answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity post a bond that only unlocks after a history of verified useful work: think of an atlas that records every crossing, where each new island outpost must first carry real cargo down the river before it earns trust. A single attacker spinning up a thousand fake identities pays the bond and the work cost a thousand times, while honest agents pay once, so faking a crowd costs as much as being one.
